plain_description.what: On the clean version 2 split, with no tree and no embedder, picks the best model per human-declared cell (dataset × domain) from training data. It checks whether this beats the single best model on held-out data, and whether model skill profiles vary reliably across the 13 MMLU-Pro categories.
plain_description.why: It checks the basic "per-cell evaluation is useful" claim on clean data, using only the declared categories.
plain_description.information: It shows whether cell-level model choice pays off at all, before any discovered tree enters. Result: done and valid. The per-cell policy beats the best single model by +2.7 points, and the skill profiles are more reliable than chance. It is a sensitivity check, not a replication. Most of the gain comes from one dataset (BBH): leaving BBH out, or looking at MMLU-Pro alone, the gain is not separated from zero, so it is descriptive. No claim is made per dataset.
